items.name: Windsor Castle
items.description: The oldest and largest occupied castle in the world, and an official residence of the King. Highlights include the State Apartments and the Gothic St George's Chapel, site of royal weddings and funerals.

items.name: Stonehenge
items.description: A UNESCO World Heritage prehistoric stone circle dating to the Neolithic age, still shrouded in mystery over its original purpose. Best visited as part of a full-day guided tour.

items.name: Oxford
items.distance: Approx. 1 hour by train from Paddington
items.description: The 'city of dreaming spires', home to the world-renowned University of Oxford. Wander cobbled lanes, ancient college courtyards, and the historic Bodleian Library, one of Europe's oldest.

items.name: Cambridge
items.distance: 48 min by train from King's Cross
items.description: Home to the historic University of Cambridge, with punting along the River Cam and stunning college architecture including King's College Chapel.

items.name: Bath
items.description: Centres on the 2,000-year-old Roman Baths and the elegant Georgian Royal Crescent. One of England's most complete historic cities.

items.name: The Cotswolds
items.description: Honey-coloured limestone villages like Bourton-on-the-Water, Bibury and Stow-on-the-Wold set among rolling English countryside. The most popular rural escape from London.
items.entryFee: Free to explore, tour costs vary

items.name: Canterbury
items.description: Home to Canterbury Cathedral, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of England's oldest and most famous Christian sites, drawing pilgrims since medieval times.

items.name: Hampton Court Palace
items.description: Henry VIII's former royal palace, with sprawling Tudor architecture, a world-famous maze, and beautifully maintained gardens along the Thames.
